scheme_name: Trainning Scheme for Horticulture Skill Development to Landless farm labour at Centre of Excelence of Department
description:
The Training Scheme for Horticulture Skill Development to Landless Farm Labour is a government initiative aimed at enhancing the skills of landless agricultural laborers in India. 

This scheme was launched in 2014 under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide skill development training to landless farm laborers in horticulture. 

The goal is to improve their employability and income potential through specialized training in various horticultural practices. 

The scheme targets the enhancement of skills in areas such as nursery management, cultivation of fruits and vegetables, post-harvest management, and marketing of horticulture products. 

The specific measurable target is to train at least 1 lakh landless farm laborers annually across various states in India. 

The training is conducted at various Centers of Excellence established by the Department of Horticulture. 

These centers are equipped with modern facilities and experienced trainers to ensure high-quality skill development. 

The benefits of the scheme include the provision of free training to participants. 

Each participant receives a stipend of ₹250 per day during the training period. 

The training duration typically ranges from 15 days to 3 months depending on the specific skill being taught. 

Participants also receive practical exposure through field visits and hands-on training in horticulture practices. 

Upon successful completion of the training, participants are provided with a certificate that enhances their employability. 

The eligibility criteria for the scheme are specific. 

Applicants must be landless agricultural laborers. 

There is no age limit specified for participation in the scheme. 

However, preference is given to individuals from marginalized communities and women. 

Income criteria are not explicitly defined but priority is given to those with lower income levels. 

Educational qualifications are also not a barrier; however, basic literacy is preferred. 

The application process for the scheme is straightforward. 

Interested candidates must approach the nearest Center of Excellence or the local Department of Horticulture office. 

They need to fill out an application form which is available at these centers. 

Required documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhar card or voter ID. 

Additionally, applicants must provide a self-declaration of their landless status. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the officials at the center. 

Selected candidates are then notified about the training schedule. 

The training sessions are conducted periodically throughout the year. 

The frequency of training sessions varies by region based on demand and resources. 

Disbursement of stipends occurs at the end of each week during the training period. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Horticulture under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

Each state has its own Department of Horticulture responsible for the execution of the scheme at the local level. 

Contact details for the Department of Horticulture can be found on the official Ministry of Agriculture website. 

The scheme has seen significant participation since its inception. 

In the year 2022 alone, approximately 1.2 lakh landless laborers were trained under this initiative. 

The success of the scheme is reflected in the increased income levels of participants. 

Many trained individuals have reported a 30% increase in their earnings after acquiring new skills. 

The scheme also contributes to the overall development of the horticulture sector in India. 

It aims to promote sustainable agricultural practices and improve food security. 

The horticulture sector is a vital part of the Indian economy, contributing around ₹3 lakh crore annually. 

By enhancing the skills of landless laborers, the scheme helps in increasing productivity in the sector. 

Furthermore, it encourages the adoption of modern techniques in horticulture. 

The scheme aligns with the government's broader vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

It also supports the National Policy for Farmers which emphasizes skill development and capacity building. 

The Training Scheme for Horticulture Skill Development is part of a larger framework of initiatives aimed at rural development. 

It complements other schemes such as the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi and the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act. 

The impact of this scheme is monitored through regular assessments and feedback from participants. 

Success stories of trained individuals are documented to inspire others. 

The government continues to refine the program based on participant feedback and changing market demands. 

Overall, the Training Scheme for Horticulture Skill Development to Landless Farm Labour represents a significant effort by the Indian government to empower rural communities. 

It provides essential skills that can lead to better livelihoods and improved quality of life for landless agricultural laborers. 

The scheme is a critical component of India's strategy to enhance agricultural productivity and rural employment. 

By focusing on skill development in horticulture, the government aims to create a more resilient agricultural workforce. 

This initiative not only benefits individuals but also contributes to the economic growth of rural areas. 

The ongoing commitment to this scheme reflects the government's dedication to supporting the agricultural sector and improving the lives of those who depend on it. 

As of October 2023, the scheme continues to be operational and is actively enrolling participants. 

The government encourages eligible individuals to take advantage of this opportunity for skill development in horticulture. 

This scheme is a testament to the importance of skill training in achieving sustainable agricultural practices and enhancing food security in India.
